sources.entry: flower - A real-time monitor and web admin for Celery task queues.

summary.one_liner: Flower is an open-source web application for monitoring and managing Celery task queue clusters in real time.
summary.what_it_does: Flower connects to a Celery broker and shows the status of Celery workers and tasks as they happen, using Celery Events. It lets you view task progress, history, arguments, start time and runtime. It offers remote control of workers: viewing stats, shutting down or restarting them, changing pool size and autoscale settings, and changing the queues they consume from. You can also see running, scheduled (ETA/countdown), reserved and revoked tasks, apply time and rate limits, and revoke or terminate tasks. Broker monitoring shows statistics for all Celery queues. It provides an HTTP API for managing the cluster over HTTP, and includes Prometheus integration and HTTP Basic Auth plus Google, GitHub, GitLab and Okta OAuth login.
use_cases: monitor Celery workers and tasks in real time
restart or scale Celery workers remotely
revoke or terminate running Celery tasks
manage Celery clusters over an HTTP API
notable: Remote control of Celery workers, including pool size, autoscale and queue changes
Task and worker inspection with time and rate limit controls
OAuth login through Google, GitHub, GitLab and Okta
Runs as a standalone celery subcommand or from a Docker image
caveats: Requires an existing Celery setup and a message broker URL
Default port is 5555 and can be changed with the port option
README does not describe security hardening for public deployment
